summary: Two authenticated T1 native workers completed four assignments across two int8 optimizer steps and a coordinator restart. Resident conversion and direct layer-bundle construction both matched the int8 oracle exactly, the maximum canonical-checkpoint relative L2 was 6.12852298785371e-8, both workers reused one model with zero warm model payload, held-out mean loss improved by 0.001623988151550293, every checkpoint bound the int8 profile in v2 weight/resume identities, and exact-FP32 restart was rejected. The final int8 adapter remained 0.011018934557552882 relative L2 from exact FP32.

guardrails.detail: Both canonical int8 checkpoints remained within 6.12852298785371e-8 relative L2 of their centralized profile oracle, below 1e-6.
Frozen held-out mean loss improved from 9.042177319526672 to 9.040553331375122.
Assignments, accepted ledgers, evaluations, and both orcacolony_lora_checkpoint_v2 records carried int8 identity; coordinator restart after step 1 preserved it and exact-FP32 reload failed closed.
Exact CPU FP32 rejects one-ULP worker-gradient changes, int8 uses separate runtime/oracle identities, and the connected final adapters differed by 0.011018934557552882 relative L2.
Resident-converted and direct-bundle workers each built once, reused the model after coordinator restart, refreshed only the adapter, and reported zero warm model payload.

findings.label: Homogeneous int8 is connected-campaign viable
findings.description: Two independent placements returned bit-exact profile gradients and aggregated through ordinary authenticated leases, canonical AdamW, evaluation, and restart.

findings.label: Placement can vary without mixing numerical profiles
findings.description: Resident conversion and direct bundle construction shared one int8 identity; exact CPU FP32 and Burn backends remained separately named and could not submit to the int8 campaign.

findings.label: Direct bundle construction materially reduces T2 startup peak
findings.description: The preserved T2 build proof reduced peak RSS through build by 66.75% versus complete resident FP32 construction followed by conversion while retaining identical int8 tensors, loss, and gradient digest.

findings.label: Small loss drift does not imply trajectory identity
findings.description: Connected and twenty-step final adapters differed from exact FP32 by 1.10% and 2.64% relative L2, respectively; cross-profile aggregation remains prohibited.

limitations: The connected qualification ran for two T1 steps on one Windows CPU host over loopback; it does not establish heterogeneous WAN throughput, remote participant reliability, or long-horizon convergence.
The T2 direct-construction result is an isolated startup/gradient measurement, not a connected T2 campaign.
Native GPU and GPU-plus-system-RAM placement were unavailable on the CPU-only PyTorch host and are not claimed; browser WebGPU remains a separately named measured profile.
Direct layer-bundle execution reduces retained/startup memory but this campaign does not prove a model larger than available system RAM.
The base model is deterministic and randomly initialized; positive TinyStories held-out movement is a use-case guardrail, not useful language-model quality.
Peak RSS is process-wide and includes Python/PyTorch allocator and runtime overhead.
